extraction.name: CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images
extraction.description: We assemble a dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed (CC) images, which we use to train a set of open diffusion models that are qualitatively competitive with Stable Diffusion 2 (SD2). This task presents two challenges: (1) high-resolution CC images lack the captions necessary to train text-to-image generative models; (2) CC images are relatively scarce. In turn, to address these challenges, we use an intuitive transfer learning technique to produce a set of high-quality synthetic captions paired with curated CC images. We then develop a data- and compute-efficient training recipe that requires as little as 3% of the LAION data (i.e., roughly 70 million examples) needed to train existing SD2 models, but obtains the same quality. These results indicate that we have a sufficient number of CC images (also roughly 70 million) for training high-quality models. Our training recipe also implements a variety of optimizations that achieve ∼3X training speed-ups, and that enable rapid model iteration. We leverage this recipe to train several high-quality text-to-image models, which we dub the CommonCanvas family. Our largest model achieves comparable performance to SD2 on human evaluation, even though we only use a CC dataset that is <3% the size of LAION and synthetic captions for training.
extraction.creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov
extraction.citeAs: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov. CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv preprint arXiv:2310.16825, 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: We assemble a dataset of Creative-Commons-licensed (CC) images. We began with the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files, as well as Flickr IDs linking to the original data. We re-scraped these images from Flickr, based on the IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. Our scraped images are very high resolution (exceeding 4K). We exclude images with non-derivative (ND) licenses. The remaining images are divided into those that can be used for commercial (C) purposes and those that cannot (non-commercial/ NC), constructing CommonCatalog-C and CommonCatalog-NC. In total, CommonCatalog contains roughly 70 million NC CC-images, of which a subset of approximately 25 million images can also be used commercially.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Almost all CC images lack the captions necessary to train a high-quality T2I model. CC images rarely have the alt-text captions necessary to train a T2I model; those that do often just include the image title or a URL.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The YFCC100M dataset, consisting of 100 million CC-licensed images and multimedia files, along with Flickr IDs linking to the original data, was used as the source. Images were re-scraped from Flickr based on these IDs.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. The remaining images were divided into commercial (C) and non-commercial (NC) datasets (CommonCatalog-C and CommonCatalog-NC). For captioning, images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the captioning process, images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels. At training time of the diffusion model, all images remain in their native resolution.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A pre-trained BLIP-2 model (specifically BLIP-2 OPT2.5B) was used to produce high-quality, synthetic captions for the curated, open-licensed CC images. This method, termed 'telephoning', leverages powerful pre-trained generative models to produce synthetic labels for an unlabeled dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: BLIP-2 captions were found to be qualitatively more descriptive than LAION-2B ground-truth alt-text captions, which often contain product names, irrelevant details, or poor grammar. Quantitatively, BLIP-2 captions showed higher quality (in terms of CLIP Score) than ground-truth captions, but at the cost of caption diversity, exhibiting reduced diversity of n-grams.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Images of people, including public figures and faces, are part of the dataset. The model's ability to synthesize individual people and iconic characters is discussed.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset addresses copyright concerns and reproducibility issues associated with web-scraped datasets like LAION-2B, which have unclear provenance and are subject to link rot. By using independently curated, open-licensed Creative-Commons images with known provenance, the dataset aims to provide a more legally sound and reproducible alternative for training generative models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The model trained on this dataset is less likely to generate iconic characters given suggestive prompts compared to SD2. It is also worse at synthesizing individual people. There is a domain shift between MS COCO captions and web-scraped conceptual captions, and the synthetic captions exhibit reduced diversity of n-grams.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The model underperformed in several categories, including faces, general photography, and paintings. The synthetic captions introduce certain performance challenges and have reduced diversity of n-grams. The YFCC100M data, from which the images were sourced, is about a decade old, meaning its CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. The dataset's generalization limits to specific categories might require users to supplement with their own datasets for fine-tuning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image diffusion models; Evaluation of text-to-image models.
